findings.title: The Cloudflare line is derived from 'both mailboxes end in @qaren.app', so the fill-in removes a real recipient while the policy and the landing pages still publish @qaren.app addresses (rc 0; only T7a catches it later)
findings.evidence: scripts/legal_variants_u8.json forks.cloudflare_clause takes the answer {all_end_with: [PRIVACY_EMAIL, SUPPORT_EMAIL], suffix '@qaren.app'}. fill_in_legal.py _answer returns all(...). This follows the literal text of UP4 A12(b). Probe probe_fill3.py (scratch copy) with PRIVACY_EMAIL privacy@qaren.app and SUPPORT_EMAIL help@gmail.com: rc 0 and the '- **Cloudflare:**' line is gone. The same policy says 'Contact: privacy@qaren.app' in s1 and s16. The landing chrome outside the regions hard-codes support@qaren.app 5 times on support.html (lines 9 meta refresh, 199 CTA, 204, 207), plus the footer of privacy.html:326 and terms.html:264, and once or more on each AR page. Mail sent to any of these addresses still passes through Cloudflare. probe_fill.py hit this case in 107 of 230 combinations: a qaren.app mailbox is published but the Cloudflare line is removed. A subdomain address (privacy@mail.qaren.app) also removes it. The published policy then omits a recipient of user email. The only backstop is T7a: SPEC_RECIPIENTS_EN includes Cloudflare (test_legal_docs_u8.py:781-784), so T7a turns red at the fill-in commit. That is the conflict the polish report raises as Q3. test_polish_a12b pins the 'both' behaviour, because it asserts the line is gone for privacy@qaren.app with help@example.com.
findings.fix: This needs an amendment to the ruling (UP4 A12(b) as written produces the false omission). While the landing chrome hard-codes support@qaren.app, keep the Cloudflare line unconditional: make the fork's answer constant true, or drop the fork and restore the plain line. At the least, derive it as 'any address ends in @qaren.app'. Change test_polish_a12b (this round's own uncommitted node) or append a node for the mixed case. This also settles Q3: T7a never turns red at the fill-in.

findings.title: A DPO contact recorded in only one language is accepted, so the EN and AR policies differ
findings.evidence: probe_fill2.py: DPO_CONTACT_DETAILS 'Jane Doe, dpo@example.com' with DPO_CONTACT_DETAILS_AR null gives rc 0. The EN policy names the officer in s1 and s16 and the AR policy does not. The reverse (AR only) also gives rc 0. The cause is the DPO_CONTACT clause's if_null '': null is never reported missing, so a forgotten _AR twin goes through silently. (HOSTING_REGIONS has the same EN/AR asymmetry, which predates this round.)
findings.fix: In _answer_placeholder_problems, refuse when exactly one of DPO_CONTACT_DETAILS and DPO_CONTACT_DETAILS_AR is non-null, and append one node.

findings.title: S7 and C3 survived as near-equivalent or equivalent mutants
findings.evidence: S7: _check_pages renders the on-disk unfilled source instead of the filled output, and 62 tests pass. Both counsel insertion points (legal_basis at privacy_policy.md:55-57 and TRANSFER_BASIS inline) are bordered by blank lines, and _check_value already refuses each out-of-subset line. So no value that the value checks accept makes a filled source unrenderable: the filled-source render branch of B2 is defence in depth and no node reaches it. C3: removing 'shownLang.current = lang' in the cache branch passes 34 tests. load() runs again only on a lang or endpoint change, when the ref differs anyway.
findings.fix: None required. Optionally add a docstring line on the S7 branch saying it is a defensive re-check.

findings.title: B10 has no guard against a stale response
findings.evidence: LegalScreen.tsx load(): with two language changes inside one request round-trip (en -> ar -> en), the late AR response sets shownLang 'ar' and the AR content while lang is 'en'. If the EN fetch then fails with no cache, errorKey is set but content is non-null, so the AR document stays on screen. The window is narrow (language changes happen in Settings), and this class of bug predates the round.
findings.fix: Optional: capture lang in a request id or ref and ignore a response whose lang is no longer current.

findings.title: The forced deviations Q1, Q2 and Q4 are confirmed, and the new answers are forced only by the UP6 checklist

summary: The polish round is sound apart from one major finding. P1 is the major one: ruling UP4 A12(b) derives the Cloudflare line from 'both PRIVACY_EMAIL and SUPPORT_EMAIL end in @qaren.app'. With one mailbox elsewhere, the fill-in exits 0 and removes Cloudflare from the policy, yet the policy itself still publishes privacy@qaren.app and the landing pages hard-code support@qaren.app outside the regions (support.html x5, the privacy and terms footers, the AR pages). The policy then omits a recipient of user email, and only T7a catches it, at the fill-in commit (the polish report's Q3). The fix is to keep the line unconditional while the page chrome hard-codes the mailbox, which needs a ruling amendment and a change to this round's a12b node. Minor findings: P2, an EN-only or AR-only DPO is accepted; P3, d3 = B with the store unpinned leaves a dangling 'the 30-day limit below' (already disclosed as Q6); P4, five unpinned behaviours, shown by surviving mutants S1, S2, S3, R1 and T5, with the nodes to add listed; P5, counsel transfer-basis wording written as list items renders garbled inline. Everything else re-measured as the polish report claims: every UP4 and UP8 item is applied in EN and AR, each new sentence matches the code it describes, 230 legitimate answer combinations fill correctly and idempotently, the F1/B1 refusals and the new refusals fire with clear messages, the 15 renderer refusals fire while the six real sources render, test changes are append-only, the backend gives T2 as the only red with 147 passed, and the full jest suite (3536 passed), tsc and eslint (0 errors) match. Of my 19 executed mutants, 12 were killed and 7 survived, 2 of them equivalent.
